paper.title_en: Development of a high-speed, high-precision beam current measurement system for HALF with beam experiment verification at HLS-II
paper.abstract_en: Advanced light sources and colliders necessitate increasingly stringent demands on the precision and data acquisition rates of beam current measurement. To address these challenges, this paper presents the development of a high-speed, high-precision beam current measurement system. The system is based on a 24-bit, 2 MHz analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and a fully pipelined field programmable gate array (FPGA), enabling high-speed, high-precision measurement of the average beam current and beam lifetime. The pipeline design is implemented throughout the signal, processing and data output stages. Comprehensive testing and analysis of both board-level and system noise have been conducted. To validate the system's performance, beam experiments were carried out at the Hefei Light Source (HLS-II). The system achieves a beam current measurement resolution better than 4 μA at a 1 kHz sampling rate and better than 1 μA at a 1 Hz sampling rate. Furthermore, it can complete a measurement of the beam lifetime within 1 s after injection. The system's high temporal resolution capability can also capture transient processes, such as beam loss. The measurement system provides essential technical support for beam commissioning and operational monitoring at the Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF) and holds significant application value for frontier charged particle accelerators.
